The big read

Monday snapshot · Oct. 5. Odds are the MMA Junkie / Oddschecker market snapshot and can move before Saturday.

Main event · Middleweight · 5 rounds
Brendan Allen27–7 · #5 · three-fight streak
VS
Christian Leroy Duncan15–2 · #10 · five-fight streak
−135 / +115Allen / Duncan · Oct. 5
75″ / 79″Reach
15–4 / 8–2UFC records

Allen’s pressure grappling has already carried him through four UFC main events. Duncan reaches this first headliner as the division’s biggest recent Elo climber, mixing switch-stance range with spinning-elbow and spinning-backfist knockouts.

The hinge: Allen must consistently close four inches of reach and force Duncan to defend takedowns. Duncan’s 57% takedown defense has to survive for 25 minutes; Allen only needs one extended grappling sequence to turn the fight.

MODEL VS. MARKET: Combat Edge’s frozen Elo model favors Duncan 52% to Allen 48%, while the market makes Allen a −135 favorite and Duncan a +115 underdog. That disagreement is a real value signal for Duncan—not a guarantee.

Price’s UFC fights

The veteran returns for one last walk after his first retirement moment was overshadowed.

Pressure points

The stories that matter beyond the headliner.

Price’s proper farewell

Niko Price says this is the end. The UFC called after his Seattle retirement went without the promised post-fight interview, and he accepted one last matchup with Leon Shahbazyan.

First meeting, not a trilogy

Andre Fili and Kai Kamaka III have never fought before. The booking is a fresh crossroads matchup between Fili’s 13 years of UFC mileage and Kamaka’s second promotional run.

GM3’s 205-pound last stand

Gerald Meerschaert moves up after five losses. Julius Walker is 1-3 in the UFC and has been stopped twice in 2026, so both carry roster pressure.

Wellmaker’s reset

Two upset losses sent Malcolm Wellmaker to American Top Team. Grappler Otari Tanzilovi is the direct test of whether that move fixed the weakness.

What they’re saying

Fight-week context from verified interviews.

Camilo sees the opening

“I think he sometimes struggles on the ground, and I see few spaces I can catch him striking, also.”Matheus Camilo · MMA Junkie Radio, Sept. 15

Wellmaker on ATT

“The coaches are really, really invested in me... The teammates are really pushing me but really welcomed me onto the team, too.”Malcolm Wellmaker · MMA Junkie Radio, Sept. 14

Price on one more

“I’m gonna end it with this one... If a golden nugget comes up, you can’t turn down a golden nugget.”Niko Price · Home of Fight, via EssentiallySports

Allen wants the top

“We’ll see if he mans up and takes the fight, or if he’s just going to stay talking.”Brendan Allen on Dricus du Plessis · MMA Junkie Radio

The contract fights

Tuesday snapshot · five three-round bouts · no published betting odds found as of Oct. 5.

Main event · Women’s bantamweight · 3 rounds
Summer Onley6–0 · FCC champion
VS
Alivia Bierley5–1 · five-fight streak
5 KO winsOnley
5 straightBierley
No oddsPublished by Oct. 5

Onley is an unbeaten FCC champion with a BJJ brown belt and five knockouts in six professional wins. Bierley walked away from a corporate VP career, won a championship two weeks later and now arrives on a five-fight streak.

The hinge: Bierley’s strength and willingness to fight through chaos must overcome Onley’s rare two-route finishing threat—one-punch power plus a proven submission base.

Model vs. market: no reputable predictive model and no published Week 9 odds were found. Combat Press picks Onley; Tapology’s community leans Onley 80% to 20%. Those are opinion signals, not betting lines.

Four pressure points

The stories that shape Tuesday’s contract decisions.

The employee audition

Everett started in the mailroom and corporate security before becoming Dana White’s runner. White says the opponent will be treated fairly despite the unusual optics.

Undefeated versus undefeated

Everett and Martin are both 4-0 and finish-first. Martin’s claim that his grappling is overlooked adds a second layer to the expected striking sprint.

LaGrange jumps a division

A natural middleweight, Preston LaGrange replaces Ivan Gnizditskity on two weeks’ notice and meets a 6-foot-4 undefeated judoka at light heavyweight.

Second chances collide

Roque Conceição was stopped on DWCS in 2025. Unbeaten Alexander Chávez is also making a second series appearance, so only one can turn the return trip into a contract case.

Underdog value board

Price-sensitive cases, ranked by realistic win path. Odds from the Oct. 5 MMA Junkie / Oddschecker snapshot. Never a guarantee.

TOP MODEL-VS.-MARKET FLAG: Christian Leroy Duncan +115. Combat Edge makes Duncan 52% while the market implies roughly 46.5% before vig. The edge is modest but meaningful.
#1
+115

Christian Leroy Duncan

Four-inch reach edge, five straight wins and the only named model disagreement on the card. Allen’s favorite status may be overpricing experience relative to this style matchup.

#2
+180

Ketlen Souza

Two wins in 2026 and a 94-second knockout give Souza the cleaner momentum. Godinez’s wrestling is real, but the −220 price may be too wide after her submission loss to Suarez.

#3
+185

Otari Tanzilovi

His grappling directly attacks Wellmaker’s 47% takedown defense. The favorite has already lost twice as a big chalk, so the market may be buying the ATT reset too early.

#4
+205

Gerald Meerschaert

Age, five losses and a move to 205 explain the price, but Walker is 1-3 in the UFC with two 2026 stoppage losses. GM3’s 29 submissions create a real scramble path.

#5
+105

Francisco Prado

All 12 wins are stoppages and Bonfim took this fight after Artur Minev withdrew. Near pick’em pricing reflects both men’s skids; Prado’s pressure makes the dog side playable.

Matchup-based upset cases

No published Week 9 odds existed on Oct. 5, so there is no honest underdog price board and no parlay.

No market, no manufactured signal: the MMA Gambling Podcast released an audio betting guide, but its page contained no written lines. Without prices, this guide ranks plausible upset routes rather than pretending to identify betting value.
#1
No line

Ozzy Martin

Tapology leans Everett 76/24, but Martin is also 4-0 with four knockouts and says his grappling is underrated. Everett’s sub-three-minute résumé has never been extended.

#2
No line

Alivia Bierley

Tapology leans Onley 80/20, yet Bierley owns five straight wins, physical strength and experience thriving through messy fights. The upset path is forcing Onley past the clean first exchange.

#3
No line

Ryuho Miyaguchi

Combat Press calls him the long shot, but six knockouts in seven wins make his kicking game a one-shot equalizer against the episode’s most touted prospect.

#4
No line

Preston LaGrange

He is undersized and short notice, but wrestling, speed and cardio are the exact tools that can neutralize Ariano’s height if the larger fighter cannot keep range.
